widgets_values: Up to 9 reference images can be connected. To skip one, bypass its group.
Up to 3 reference videos (2-15 s each, 15 s total). These define camera movement style and motion logic.
Up to 3 reference audio clips (must be paired with an image or video, 15 s total). These set rhythm, dialogue and ambient sound.

Reference: image 1 = character identity (purple hair, face reference), image 2 =
outfit reference.

She wears the outfit from image 2, dancing in a crowded nightclub — pulsing
colored lights, dense fog/haze catching the light beams, a packed dance floor
around her, bass-driven energy.

[0s–4s] Medium shot, she moves fluidly to the beat, hair swinging with her
movement, colored strobe light sweeping across her face and body in rhythm.

[4s–8s] Camera circles slowly around her as she dances, other dancers blurred and
out of focus around her, she remains the sharp focal point, lights flashing in
sync with the music's rhythm.

[8s–12s] Close-up on her face, eyes closed, lost in the moment, lights flaring
and pulsing behind her, hair catching the light as she moves.

Style: high-energy nightclub cinematography, saturated colored lighting (magenta,
cyan, deep blue), lens flare and light streaks, shallow depth of field isolating
her from the crowd, confident and immersive dance energy.

Audio: pulsing club music/bass, ambient crowd noise, energetic and rhythmic
throughout.

Do not include: text, subtitles, watermark, logos, changes to her identity or the
outfit.

SINGLE-PASS (fastest):
Leave Stage 2 bypassed. In the Resolution Selector choose the size you want -
0.9 is recommended, which outputs 720p directly.

TWO-PASS (higher quality):
If you enable Stage 2, lower the Stage 1 resolution first - 0.4 is recommended.
Pass 1 runs fast at low resolution, then pass 2 re-samples at fewer steps and
raises the resolution. Tune it to your hardware and needs (too high hurts speed).

TIP: when running locally, leave Stage 2 off while you roll seeds. Once you get
a result you like, lock the seed and turn Stage 2 on to strengthen it.
